feedback: This candidate changes three things from iteration 0, each tied to that race's evidence. (1) The sensor array is widened to x = -0.03 to +0.03 m in 15 mm steps, with 16 mm footprints. Iteration 0 showed the s-bend and slalom ending off track with max_error about 0.062 to 0.063 m, above the 0.06 m limit, and 1.55 to 2.0 line-loss events per run, which points to tape being lost at lateral errors the old +/-0.02 m array could not cover. (2) kd rises from 0.4 to 0.8 to test whether more damping reduces steering_oscillation, which was about 0.27 on the oval and s-bend in iteration 0. (3) base_speed drops from 1.6 to 1.5 to reduce slip on the sharp sections. The oval finished at 1.9 s in iteration 0, so there is time margin. The sensor weights stay at (-2, -1, 0, 1, 2), so the signal scale is unchanged even though the physical spacing is wider. Nothing about this candidate's performance is stated here; the race will show it. Plan the next revision from the telemetry as follows. If line_loss_events fall but max_error still exceeds 0.06 on the s-bend or slalom, the array is working and the next lever is kp or kd on those sections. If steering_oscillation stays above about 0.2 with kd 0.8, raise kd further in steps of 0.2 before changing kp. If the oval no longer completes or completion_time rises well above 2 s, return base_speed to 1.6 and keep the sensor change. Approving this now is right for an early exploration iteration: the change is valid, specific and evidence-based, and the race will show whether the wider array addresses the main failure mode.

If the oval fails to complete or completion_time rises above about 2.2 s, return base_speed to 1.6 and keep the sensor change. Basis: the oval finished in 1.9 s with 40% completion at base_speed 1.6, so speed is the lever for finish time.
